statements.text: Rowan attended 12 goal-eligible therapy sessions between January 5–30, 2026: 5 individual (Jan 5, 14, 19, 21, 26), 5 group (Jan 6, 12, 19, 22, 29), and 2 family (Jan 9, 30). These sessions fell on 11 distinct days (January 19 had both a group and an individual session).

Eight encounters were attended but excluded from the therapy count: two medication management visits (Jan 13, HG-E106; Jan 30, HG-E120) — medication does not count toward the goal; two contacts held without Rowan present (Jan 16, HG-E109, a collateral contact with the partner only; Jan 23, HG-E114, a care coordination call Rowan did not join); two no-shows (Jan 8, HG-E103, individual; Jan 27, HG-E116, group); one clinic cancellation (Jan 15, HG-E108, group cancelled due to staff illness); and one patient cancellation (Jan 28, HG-E117, individual, personal scheduling conflict).

Several document features require attention to avoid duplicate or inflated counts. The appointment desk export lists nine encounters in a single document (HG-E101 through HG-E109); the outpatient attendance and disposition extract lists four (HG-E113, HG-E116, HG-E117, HG-E118); and the skills group activity record covers two dates (HG-E113 and HG-E118) — each of these is a multi-visit document, not a separate visit, and each encounter is counted only once. For the January 19 group session (HG-E110), the original attendance roster showed an incorrect departure time of 11:30; a correction filed January 20 established 11:15 as Rowan's actual departure, and a cover sheet received January 26 is a copy of that roster adding no new information — neither document creates an additional session. The January 9 family session (HG-E104) has an addendum from the co-facilitator and a scheduling support log (a pre-visit planned document); neither represents a separate visit. January 19 legitimately has two counted sessions — group (HG-E110) and individual (HG-E111), the latter added same-day after Rowan became distressed in group — so the two sessions on one day are not a duplicate. The January 26 individual session (HG-E115) has two clinician records that disagree on start time (09:00 or 09:10) and duration (50 or 40 minutes); attendance is confirmed by both, so it counts as one session, but the exact creditable minutes remain unresolved. A billing record exists for the January 27 no-show (HG-E116) but that encounter is not counted. An unnumbered outbound phone call in the scheduling log has no date and no patient contact and is not counted.

statements.text: At intake (January 5), Rowan presented with several weeks of low mood, reduced interest, fragmented sleep, difficulty starting tasks, and marked anxiety-driven avoidance of work communication. Through mid-January (January 6–16), avoidance of work messages persisted, sleep remained interrupted, and daytime fatigue reinforced avoidance; the clinician noted some improvement in depressive symptoms by January 16 but flagged ongoing avoidance and inconsistent sleep. On January 19, anxiety escalated acutely during group when workplace return was discussed. Through late January (January 21–26), avoidance continued in more specific forms—drafting but not sending a message, repeatedly editing it, postponing scheduling a follow-up call—while sleep remained uneven, worsening on nights with repetitive work-related thoughts. By January 30, Rowan reported fewer days of pervasive low mood than at intake and mood felt less persistently low, but anxiety about work contact and variable sleep persisted.

The individual contact on January 19 (HG-E111) was added because Rowan became acutely anxious during the group session when discussion turned to returning to the workplace, said the amount of discussion felt difficult to manage, and requested additional help.
